Unescaped server and remote error strings reach the changed line from header.component.ts, settings-page.component.ts and file-list.component.ts. Angular's built-in sanitizer blocks script execution but not markup injection or text loss.

findings.fix_hint: revert to `{{ notif.text }}`; if the version notice needs a clickable link, add a separate `url` field to Notification and render an <a> for it in the template
findings.problem: The change from `{{ notif.text }}` to `[innerHTML]="notif.text"` makes the browser parse every notification string as HTML. Some of those strings come from outside the app: `status.server.errorMessage` (header.component.ts:49), `status.controller.latestRemoteScanError` passed through STATUS_REMOTE_SERVER_ERROR (header.component.ts:96, localization.ts:15-16), `reaction.errorMessage` (settings-page.component.ts:170/239/257) and `result.errorMessage` passed through Bulk.ERROR (file-list.component.ts:554). None of them is escaped. No Localization template contains markup (localization.ts:15-19, 74-77), so nothing needed HTML rendering. The only effect is that these strings are now read as markup. Angular's DomSanitizer removes scripts and event handlers, but it still allows tags such as `<a href>`, `<img src=https://...>` and styling elements. A remote-server or SSH error string can therefore insert a working link or a tracking image into the app UI. That is content injection, not script execution. Any text that looks like a tag is also deleted: a path such as `/data/<show name>` or an SSH stderr line like `<user>@host` loses that part. Characters like `&lt;` are decoded, so the notification shows different text than was sent. This also breaks the `.text !==` change detection in header.component.ts:54/98, which compares the raw strings while the UI shows a sanitized version. Nearby code works the other way: confirm-modal.service.ts:33 escapes HTML before inserting it. The user's CLAUDE.md also forbids rendering user-supplied content through innerHTML.

findings.why_it_matters: Error text controlled by the remote server is rendered as HTML in the app shell, which allows link and image injection, and error messages containing angle brackets show up truncated or changed.

findings.problem: The hunk changes `{{ notif.text }}` (Angular text interpolation, which HTML-escapes its value) to `[innerHTML]="notif.text"`, which parses the value as markup. `notif.text` is attacker-reachable: `Controller.__handle_extract_command` / `__handle_delete_command` in src/python/controller/controller.py (e.g. line 833: `"File '{}' in state {} cannot be extracted".format(command.filename, ...)`) interpolate the remote file name directly into error strings with no HTML sanitization; the bulk-command path only path-traversal-checks file names (src/python/web/handler/controller.py `_check_path_safe`), not HTML content. That error string flows through bulk-command.service.ts `errorMessage` into file-list.component.ts `_showNotification(Notification.Level.DANGER, Localization.Bulk.ERROR(result.errorMessage...))`, into a `Notification` shown via `NotificationService`, and is rendered here. Since remote file/torrent names are effectively attacker-controlled content, a crafted filename (e.g. containing `<a href=...>`, `<style>`, or other markup) now gets parsed as HTML in the notification bell instead of being escaped as plain text.
findings.title: Auto-escaped interpolation replaced with raw [innerHTML] binding on notification text
findings.why_it_matters: This removes a protection (automatic HTML-escaping) on a value reachable from attacker-controlled remote file names, replacing it with a raw markup sink. Angular's [innerHTML] binding does run through Angular's built-in DomSanitizer (which strips <script> tags and on* event-handler attributes), so classic inline-script execution is mitigated by default — but the sanitizer still permits many tags/attributes (links, styling, images), enabling content spoofing, phishing-style notification text, or UI redress, and the security guarantee now depends entirely on the sanitizer's correctness (which has had historical bypasses) rather than on simple text escaping.

agent_notes: Blast radius: notification-bell.component.html renders every Notification in the app. Producers I read: header.component.ts (server error, remote-scan waiting, remote-scan error), file-list.component.ts (bulk action results and errors), settings-page.component.ts (config restart and config save errors), version-check.service.ts (new-version message containing a GitHub URL).

Trust boundary: latestRemoteScanError comes from the remote seedbox, which is outside the local trust boundary. errorMessage strings come from the backend. The GitHub html_url is checked only by prefix regex. Before this diff, all of these were rendered unconditionally as text.

Protection change: Angular's DomSanitizer still blocks script and on* handler execution by default, so I did not demonstrate direct XSS. The guarantee moved from 'never parsed as HTML' to 'sanitized by the framework default'. Link, image and markup injection is possible today.
Likely motive: making the version-check URL clickable. If so, a structured link field on Notification does this without parsing arbitrary text as HTML.
No API, schema or migration impact, and no performance concern (the sanitizer cost per notification is negligible).
Verdict: not shippable as-is. Revert to text interpolation, or replace this binding with structured rich content.

findings.fix_hint: Revert to `{{ notif.text }}`. If rich text (such as a clickable version link) is needed, add a separate structured field (for example `notif.link`) rendered with a template anchor, and do not parse arbitrary text as HTML.
findings.problem: Before this change, `{{ notif.text }}` used text interpolation. That guaranteed every notification string was shown as plain text and never parsed as HTML. The change to `[innerHTML]="notif.text"` means every notification is now parsed as HTML. Safety now rests only on Angular's built-in sanitizer (a library default), not on the template. Several notification texts come from outside the app: (1) `status.server.errorMessage` at src/angular/src/app/pages/main/header.component.ts:49; (2) `status.controller.latestRemoteScanError`, interpolated by Localization.Notification.STATUS_REMOTE_SERVER_ERROR (src/angular/src/app/common/localization.ts:15-16) and shown at header.component.ts:96-106. This string comes from the remote seedbox's scan/SSH output; (3) `result.errorMessage` from the bulk API in src/angular/src/app/pages/files/file-list.component.ts:552-554; (4) `reaction.errorMessage` in src/angular/src/app/pages/settings/settings-page.component.ts:170/239/257; (5) the GitHub `html_url` in src/angular/src/app/services/utils/version-check.service.ts:60-78. That URL is checked only for a `https://github.com/` prefix, so `https://github.com/"><a href=...>` passes. Angular's sanitizer removes `<script>` and `on*` handlers, but it keeps `<a href>`, `<img src>` (remote fetch and tracking), formatting markup and misleading phishing-style content. A compromised or hostile remote server that returns an error like `<a href="https://evil">Click to re-authenticate</a>` now gets a clickable link inside a trusted DANGER notification. The same change breaks ordinary messages. Any error containing `<...>` (for example `No such file <path>` or `Permission denied <user@host>`) is dropped or mangled, and the sanitizer logs a warning in dev mode. The repo's own convention runs the other way: confirm-modal.service.ts:33 has an explicit `escapeHtml` for its innerHTML use. The user's global CLAUDE.md security rules also forbid rendering user-supplied content through innerHTML.

Script execution is now blocked only by the framework sanitizer's default. Link and image injection plus broken rendering of error text are possible today.
